newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: CRICKET-HALF A MILLION ACCLAIM BANGLADESH TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HALF A MILLION ACCLAIM BANGLADESH TRIUMPH.

text.p: An estimated half a million Bangladeshis turned out at a mass reception here on Monday to acclaim the national team after they won the International Cricket Council (ICC) trophy in Malaysia.

Bangladesh emerged as unbeaten champions by beating Kenya in Sunday's final of the limited overs tournament in Kuala Lumpur, staged to find three qualifiers from among the non test-playing countries for the 1999 World Cup in England.
The final victory added to Bangladesh's laurels after their semifinal win over Scotland on Wednesday secured the team's place in the next World Cup.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, leaving for Mecca in Saudi Arabia later on Monday to perform the Islamic pilgrimage Hajj, led the mass reception for whom she called the "Bengal tigers".

"Our victory in the ICC tournament is the most precious gift for us since the country's 1971 independence," an emotion-charged Hasina told the frenzied crowd at Dhaka's Manik Miah Avenue, overlooking the sprawling parliament house.
Hasina announced that the Bangladesh coach, former West Indies opener Gordon Greenidge, would be granted Bangladeshi nationality in recognition of his efforts.

Greenidge responded by saying that the victory was of the 120 million people of Bangladesh and that he looked forward to the 1999 World Cup where Bangladesh would play initially in a group also including south Asian test sides India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
The reception added much colour to celebrations on Monday to mark the first day of the Bengali New Year 1404, the prime minister said.
"We are enjoying so many things today...I am just spellbound," she said.
Eralier, Hasina handed flowers and prizes to members and officials of the Bangladesh team, headed by capitain Arkam Khan, and joined a chorus with leading Bangladeshi singers on the reception dais.
Security agents, intelligence officials and witnesses estimated that at least 500,000 people turned out at the reception.
The event was broadcast live on the state-run television.
"It was the biggest public showing after the victory celebratiuons following the 1971 independence," said organiser Mofazzal Hussain Maya, a member of parliament.
Sport and Youth Minister Obaidul Kader said Bangladesh made a new hisory "as the Bengal tigers defeated the African lions".
